items.name: JSON Wire Browser Lab

items.headline: What survives a round-trip?
question: Inspect browser JSON decoding,
parsing and re-encoding separately.
items.result_label: A parsed value can survive a round-trip
limits: Decoding, parsing and encoding differ
Not a semantic correctness guarantee
items.details: A browser-local workbench separates UTF-8 decoding, JSON parsing and re-encoding, with fixed byte fixtures and a frozen Python reference. locally, with its full error report.
items.result_label: Test errors · One fit, four views

Int8 storage is not a speed benchmark
items.details: One from-scratch fit on BANKING77 is evaluated as float/int8 storage with raw/calibrated probabilities: four representations, not four trained models. items.name: Split Boundary Audit · Group Planner
items.alt: Split Boundary Audit Group Planner: keep declared groups and exact-text connections together across train, validation and test. All records retained; greedy planning is not optimal and does not certify statistical independence.
items.headline: Keep groups together.
question: Plan train, validation and test splits,
then export records and review warnings.
limits: Greedy planning is not optimal
No independence or semantic guarantee
items.details: A local browser planner keeps caller-declared groups and groups connected by exact text together across train, validation and test, then exports the full plan and assigned records for the included Python auditor. It preserves every record, conflicting labels and achieved-ratio deviations. The 36-record synthetic example has 12 declared groups and 10 connected units; an 80/10/10 target yields 30/3/3 records, with one normalization candidate and one conflicting-label set retained for review. Normalized matches are candidates only. A retained counterexample shows the single-pass greedy planner is not globally optimal. Group provenance is supplied by the caller; a CLEAR audit does not prove statistical independence or absence of semantic leakage. Original Apache-2.0 code and synthetic examples; no model or external dataset. items.name: Annotation Pair Review
items.alt: Annotation Pair Review: 100% conditional agreement can cover just one of twelve synthetic records. Browser-local manual review keeps disagreements, abstentions and unfinished work visible. Agreement is not accuracy; no autosave.
items.headline: Agreement needs coverage.
question: Compare two annotation files,
then review each record manually.
limits: Agreement is not accuracy
No autosave · Export to keep work
items.details: A browser-local workbench shows conditional label agreement beside coverage, keeping disagreements, abstentions and unfinished records visible for manual final decisions. The partial synthetic example reaches 100% agreement with only 1 of 12 records labelled by both roles; the default example has 4/12 coverage and 2/4 identical labels (50%). These are scripted role annotations, not independent human annotators, accuracy or gold labels. Full inventory, taxonomy and record order must match; no intersection-only merging or automatic adjudication. The tab does not autosave: refresh loses unsaved work. Downloaded snapshots can restore a review and contain full original texts and notes; review them before sharing. Checksums establish consistency, not authenticity. No model, training or measured adoption. [Public workbench, source & reproduction](https://huggingface.co/spaces/WideChaos/annotation-pair-review) · [English write-up](https://widechaos.cn/blog/annotation-pair-review-en) · [中文说明](https://widechaos.cn/blog/annotation-pair-review-zh).

items.name: Local Label Queue
items.alt: Local Label Queue: twelve abstentions can produce 100% reviewed progress with zero assigned labels. Browser-local manual text labeling preserves labels, abstentions and unfinished work. No autosave or label-quality judgment.
items.headline: Reviewed with no labels.
question: Label text or record an abstention,
then export every source record.
limits: Review progress is not label quality
No autosave · Download a checkpoint
items.details: A browser-local manual text-labeling queue keeps labelled, abstained and unfinished records separate and preserves every source text, id, group and annotation in exports. In the synthetic all-abstained example, all 12 records are reviewed but zero labels are assigned. The running demo instead has 2 labelled, 1 abstained and 9 unfinished records; revision 5 counts edits, not reviewed records. These authored examples have no gold labels or independently verified human annotators. No model, training, automatic quality check or measured adoption. There is no autosave: refresh loses unsaved work. Download a checkpoint first; restoration requires a verified preview and explicit full-session replacement, with no merge. Exports contain full source texts and annotations, so review before sharing. Hashes establish consistency, not signatures, encryption or authenticity. [Public queue, source & reproduction](https://huggingface.co/spaces/WideChaos/local-label-queue) · [English write-up](https://widechaos.cn/blog/local-label-queue-en) · [中文说明](https://widechaos.cn/blog/local-label-queue-zh).

items.name: Prediction Metric Desk
items.alt: Prediction Metric Desk: a synthetic 75% conditional accuracy score is three of four evaluated records, while known-label coverage is four of seven. Retain missing, abstained, invalid and duplicate outputs. Saved predictions only; no new model training.
items.headline: Which records got counted?
question: Audit saved classification outputs,
keeping gaps and invalid rows visible.
limits: Synthetic example · Different denominators
Completion bounds are not confidence limits
items.details: A browser-local classification-result audit keeps the full inventory beside missing predictions, abstentions, duplicate IDs and invalid rows. In the eight-record synthetic fault example, conditional accuracy is 3/4 (75%), known-label coverage is 4/7 and total decision coverage is 5/8: different denominators, not interchangeable scores. Hypothetical completion bounds are not forecasts or confidence intervals. Saved BANKING77 predictions are recalculated, not a new model, inference, calibration run or blind benchmark; seven normalized train/test overlaps remain. No automatic repair, renormalization, clipping or invented gold labels. Full source texts and predictions appear in exports; review before sharing. Memory-only, no autosave or checkpoint restoration; refresh clears work. Hash consistency does not prove authenticity or gold-label quality. Code and synthetic fixtures are Apache-2.0; BANKING77 original and derived data retain CC BY 4.0 attribution. The standalone App passed the owner release gate; Hub embedding remained unverified in the original Edge context, with no established cause. [Standalone audit desk](https://widechaos-prediction-metric-desk.static.hf.space/index.html) · [HF source, methods & licenses](https://huggingface.co/spaces/WideChaos/prediction-metric-desk). · [English write-up](https://widechaos.cn/blog/prediction-metric-desk-en) · [中文说明](https://widechaos.cn/blog/prediction-metric-desk-zh)

items.name: Bike Hour Forecast
items.alt: Bike Hour Forecast: browser-local saved-weight inference on historical 2011–2012 system-level rental counts; 4,258 eligible test targets and 118 omitted targets. Not station availability or current-city validation.
items.summary: Estimate the next historical rental hour and compare two simple baselines locally.
limits: 118 test targets excluded for incomplete history
System-level 2011–2012 counts; no current-city or station availability validation
items.details: One 1,185-parameter network trained for 40 CPU epochs; epoch 20 was selected using validation only. The browser runs saved weights on 24 consecutive hourly counts and exports all inputs and predictions beside two untrained baselines. On the same 4,258 eligible test targets, MAE is 33.8476 versus 86.9054 and 80.9385; 118 of 4,376 test targets were omitted for incomplete history. The largest retained error predicts 509.01 against truth 114. Source data have 165 absent nominal hours, with no zero-fill or UTC/DST reconstruction. Rolling forecasts may use observed earlier validation/test counts, windows overlap, and source data were seen before the protocol. No historical-blind, uncertainty, stronger-baseline, current-city, station-availability, production or adoption claim. Today’s release runs saved weights; it is not new training. Code is Apache-2.0; UCI data and derived weights/results are CC BY 4.0 with full attribution. [Public HF source & methods](https://huggingface.co/spaces/WideChaos/bike-hour-forecast) · [Exact release](https://huggingface.co/spaces/WideChaos/bike-hour-forecast/commit/12485db6742972da6589e0ae3454657255b5fb24). · [English write-up](https://widechaos.cn/blog/bike-hour-forecast-en) · [中文说明](https://widechaos.cn/blog/bike-hour-forecast-zh)

items.name: CPU Character Router · Failed abstention threshold
items.alt: CPU Character Router: all six synthetic out-of-domain test requests were falsely accepted by a validation-selected abstention rule. Local NumPy CPU model only; no hosted App or verified provider integration.
items.summary: Inspect a failed abstention rule in a small local CPU classifier.
limits: Synthetic templates; no open-world rejection guarantee
Local NumPy CPU CLI; no hosted App or verified provider
items.details: One zero-initialized linear character classifier was fitted for 300 CPU epochs on 96 original synthetic requests, using 4,096 hashed character 1–3-gram features. All 204 records and every validation/test output are retained. The validation-selected 0.4 threshold achieved 44 correct among 47 accepted validation requests, then 43 correct among 52 accepted test requests. Known-route test accuracy was 44/48, while all six out-of-domain test requests were falsely accepted (three per language). The soup-recipe request was accepted as notes at about 0.486 maximum softmax; route preference is not calibrated confidence or membership. Templates were author-written and visible; grouped splits do not establish human blindness, semantic independence, general bilingual understanding or production safety. This release replays saved JSON weights with local NumPy; it is not a new fit, hosted App, verified Transformers/Inference Provider integration or executed tool action. Code, synthetic data and weights are original Apache-2.0 work; NumPy has separate terms. Full public Raw contents and saved-model CPU replay were verified by the release owner; the native HF download menu has no successful file-download receipt and remains a separate unverified gate. [Exact model release & evidence](https://huggingface.co/WideChaos/char-router-abstention-study/commit/bd2a30de287fe419b7d31838b40f5ae4d2d70061). items.name: Forecast Interval Lab
items.alt: Forecast Interval Lab: the nominal 90% interval covered 91.45% overall but 86.11% in October; all 364 misses retained. Historical rental counts, no future coverage guarantee.
items.summary: Inspect hourly rental intervals and the months their overall coverage hides.
limits: Historical system rentals; no station availability forecast
One saved CPU model; no future-hour or monthly coverage guarantee
items.details: A local browser lab using one original November 4 CPU point fit: 40 epochs, 1,185 parameters, Q1-selected epoch 39 and 2,134 Q2 calibration errors. Three nominal levels reuse that single fit; this publication is not new training. The fixed 90% interval covered 3,894/4,258 eligible test hours (91.4514%), with all 364 misses retained (76 below, 288 above); September reached 87.6389% and October 86.1111%. Nominal 95% reached 94.8098% overall and nominal 80% reached 82.4566%, without post-test retuning. Full 17,379-row source and 1,722 omitted targets, including 118 test targets, remain; missing nominal hours are not filled and UTC/DST is not reconstructed. Rolling one-step contexts use actual earlier observations, not a recursive six-month forecast. Overlap and seasonal shift do not establish exchangeability, per-input probability or future coverage. Known historical UCI system rental totals do not measure station availability, unmet demand or current-city validity; no blind-test or adoption claim. Browser-memory computation supports finite/unbounded exact-rank arithmetic and exports complete inputs; no inference API or autosave. Code/docs are original Apache-2.0; UCI source and derived weights/calibration/results/figure retain CC BY 4.0 attribution, with method references separately cited. The release owner verified five complete actual report downloads and public-copy replay; 57 Raw text readbacks, three matching LFS pointers and an acquired figure are not 61 native source downloads. items.name: Airfoil Split Lab
items.alt: Airfoil Split Lab: compare training pools with different condition-proxy exposure; 237 of 603 reused paired comparisons get worse, including the default case. No engineering noise certification.
items.summary: Compare noise predictions when related condition measurements enter training.
items.result_label: Seen-proxy pool has larger absolute error
limits: Condition proxies are not verified experiment IDs
Changed coverage and normalizers; no isolated causal or compliance claim
items.details: One original November 4 experiment trained six 169-parameter CPU networks for 120 epochs each: two equal 843-row training pools and seeds 17/41/73, sharing 274 validation and 201 test cases. This delivery reuses those fixed models, not new training. Pool B replaces 185 rows (658 shared) and sees other frequencies from all 27 test condition proxies; pool A sees none. Four non-frequency feature tuples are proxies, not verified run IDs or physical independence. Mean seed MAEs are A 2.644575 dB and B 2.323152 dB, but all 237 worse paired outcomes among 603 remain (86/66/85); the same 201 cases are reused, not 603 independent samples or an ensemble/significance estimate. Default source row 29 is a negative case for B under seed 17, selected by source ordinal rather than a winning outcome. Coverage and training normalizers change together, so this does not isolate overlap causality or establish unseen-condition generalization. All 1,503 source rows, six outputs, 3,800 method predictions and provenance remain. Units are scaled sound-pressure dB, not dBA, pressure, energy or engineering compliance. Known data/targets predate the protocol; the UCI binary-angle metadata discrepancy is retained. Browser-memory inputs are lost on refresh; full exports include parameters, hashes check consistency rather than authenticity, and no universal browser privacy claim is made. Apache-2.0 code/docs; Brooks/Pope/Marcolini/UCI source and derived artifacts retain CC BY 4.0, NASA-RP-1218 is cited rather than implemented. The release owner verified four final native JSON files against original DOM reports and public-copy scalar checks; 51 Raw bodies, three LFS pointers and two scientific images are not 56 native source downloads. Current mobile viewport validation is not established; original local mobile checks are historical. [Open browser lab](https://widechaos-airfoil-split-lab.static.hf.space/index.html) · [Exact release, full results & licenses](https://huggingface.co/spaces/WideChaos/airfoil-split-lab/commit/8ff0d17f86ce414c7eb4fba347024d443845a80e). items.name: Wine Domain Transfer
items.alt: Wine Domain Transfer: compare six saved red- and white-source models and two constants; familiar-source models lose in 1,585 of 3,969 reused comparisons. Not tasting or health certification.
items.summary: Compare red- and white-source models on the same wine records.
items.result_label: Familiar-source model has larger absolute error
limits: Numeric sensory scores are ordinal; input groups are not producer IDs
Equal budgets do not isolate causal shift or establish tasting certification
items.details: One original November 4 experiment trained six 313-parameter CPU models for 100 epochs each: red- and white-source fits with seeds 17/41/73, equal 923-row fit budgets and 335 own-source validation rows per domain. This delivery reuses those saved models, not new training. All 6,497 source records, 5,318 exact input groups and 1,179 duplicate-excess rows remain; two groups cross source color. Across 341 red and 982 white test cases, familiar-source models have lower mean seed MAE, yet lose in 1,585 of 3,969 reused seed/case pairs (321 red, 1,264 white). Reused pairs are not independent samples or an ensemble/significance estimate. Red-target mean MAEs are red 0.476144 and white 0.746975 score points; white-target means are red 0.649987 and white 0.586350. The white-source model on red records also loses to its own analytic constant (0.636872); two fit-mean baselines are not extra neural fits. Default red:0002 is the lowest red-test ordinal, chosen before model predictions: gold 5, seed-17 red prediction 5.365765 versus white 4.872778, so the familiar-source model is worse. All six outputs, 10,584 method predictions, 192 metric groups including empty-support nulls, full normalizers and provenance remain inspectable. Equal row/update budgets do not isolate source-shift causality: support, duplicates, normalizers, quality distributions and own-domain validation differ. Exact input tuples are not winery IDs or proof of independence; data/targets were audited before the protocol, not a historical blind test. Quality is an ordinal sensory median from at least three experts; numeric spacing is a modelling assumption. Individual chemical units are unspecified; outputs are not clipped, and observed test bounds do not guarantee arbitrary inputs. Not wine health, safety, tasting, certification or production/generalization assurance. Browser-memory inputs are lost on refresh; deliberate exports contain all inputs, and hashes check consistency rather than authenticity or universal privacy. Original code/docs Apache-2.0; Cortez/Cerdeira/Almeida/Matos/Reis (2009), UCI DOI 10.24432/C56S3T source and derived weights/normalizers/catalog/results/figures retain CC BY 4.0. Source-paper metadata is cited, not a full-paper reproduction claim. The release owner verified five actual complete native JSON reports against DOM and all 30 neural outputs by public-copy scalar replay; 58 Raw texts and eight binary LFS pointers are not 66 native source downloads. Current 375/390 public viewport checks belong to the release owner's measured scope. [Open browser lab](https://widechaos-wine-domain-transfer.static.hf.space/index.html) · [Exact release, full results & licenses](https://huggingface.co/spaces/WideChaos/wine-domain-transfer/commit/2431a336acc4cef56f12b22a90bc77baed8c6863). items.name: Carry Memory Lab
items.alt: Carry Memory Lab: resetting a tiny addition model gives 14 for 1+15. Padding raises bit accuracy to 61/65 without fixing the integer. Finite probes do not prove unrestricted addition.
items.summary: Compare retained and reset hidden states in a tiny addition model.
limits: Higher bit accuracy can leave the whole integer wrong
One saved fit; reset is not an optimized memoryless baseline
items.details: One original November 4–5 saved training and independent verification used a 106-parameter tanh RNN: two inputs, eight hidden coordinates and two outputs, seed 329, 80 epochs with selected epoch 80. This release is not new training. Both modes use the same weights; resetting every bit changes the hidden-state distribution rather than fitting an optimized memoryless baseline. The preselected held-out default 1 + 15 at width 6 gives recurrent 16 versus reset 14, with 7/7 versus 3/7 correct bits. Padding the same operands to 64 bits raises reset bit accuracy to 61/65 but leaves its integer wrong at 14; values are unchanged while sequence length grows. Every bit, terminal carry, hidden coordinate, logit and exact reference remains inspectable, without correcting wrong neural answers. Saved finite evaluation retains all 64,856 unique cases and all 58,566 reset integer failures: recurrent 64,856/64,856 versus reset 6,290/64,856. Suite memberships, reverse and padding views overlap; 64,882 memberships are not independent cases, and 17 fit stress views are explicitly tagged. Primary union has 64,499 distinct declared cases. Wider numeric ranges and lengths change together; fixed probes are not an unrestricted addition theorem, blind benchmark or population guarantee. Reference bits and true carry never enter the RNN, and no hidden coordinate is established as a causal carry neuron. Synthetic operands remain canonical decimal strings with BigInt for 64-bit operands and 65-bit sums; probabilities are uncalibrated. Use exact arithmetic for real financial or engineering calculations. All original synthetic data, code, weights, results and figures are Apache-2.0 by Renchao Wu; D2L BPTT is a principle reference, without copied code/prose/figures or a literal identity/no-bias reproduction claim. Page-memory edits are lost on clear/refresh; deliberate exports include full input and state, while hashes check consistency rather than authenticity or universal browser privacy. The release owner verified five actual final native reports and public-copy scalar replay of 514 mode-bit steps and 4,112 hidden coordinates; 49 Raw texts and 13 binary LFS pointers are not 62 native source downloads. Full saved-result replays and release-owner measured 375/390 browser checks retain their original scopes. [Open browser lab](https://widechaos-carry-memory-lab.static.hf.space/index.html) · [Exact release, full results & licenses](https://huggingface.co/spaces/WideChaos/carry-memory-lab/commit/60cf66fc3344886646bcb27e7340bf3010ba2d11). [English write-up](https://widechaos.cn/blog/carry-memory-lab-en) · [中文详解](https://widechaos.cn/blog/carry-memory-lab-zh).

items.name: Tensor Header Desk
items.alt: Tensor Header Desk: inspect declared Safetensors names, shapes and byte ranges locally. Altered payloads can pass header layout checks; this does not authenticate weights.
items.summary: Inspect declared tensor names, shapes and byte ranges before loading weights.
limits: Tensor data is not decoded or authenticated
Bounded profile; no model quality, licence or downstream safety certification
items.details: A bounded browser inspector reads a selected local Safetensors file's length prefix and supported JSON header to check declared names, shapes, dtype widths and byte ranges. It does not decode tensor values, run inference, train a model or authenticate the full file. The existing Char Router example retains its earlier 12,291 F64 scalars and original out-of-domain abstention failure; serialization is not new training. The included original and payload-bitflip examples have the same header digest and pass layout checks even though their tensor data differ. Truncated, overlapping-range and invalid-JSON examples remain invalid; unknown dtype remains outside this tool's profile. Limits include a 1 MiB header, 10,000 tensors and nesting depth 32. All 22 dtype widths describe byte arithmetic, not numerical decoding. Finite 320-fixture comparison with official Safetensors 0.8.0 and NumPy 2.5.4 retains three reader differences (duplicate-name policy, header cap and tensor cap); the historical independent 123-fixture review has a separate denominator. Agreement is not complete equivalence or a security proof. The final same-Space hosting adaptation uses same-origin JSON carriers for six intentionally fully fetched public examples, then applies the unchanged bounded inspector; selected local files retain prefix/header-only reads. Package pins establish consistency, not independent authenticity. The release owner verified six complete final native example reports and their source context, with independent Python checks of nine descriptor rows plus same-implementation public-inspector replay; this display round does not repeat downloads. Network/cancellation/elapsed-time and malformed-carrier checks include controlled loader/DOM tests, separate from native browser evidence. Current release-owner measured 375/390 layout and horizontal keyboard scrolling retain their original scope. Explicit reports may contain private tensor names and metadata; Clear is not secure erasure. No selected-file upload or browser storage is introduced. Original code, synthetic fixtures, prior model, results and figures are Apache-2.0 by Renchao Wu; upstream reference and dependency terms remain separate. [Open browser tool](https://widechaos-tensor-header-desk.static.hf.space/index.html) · [Exact release, full results & licenses](https://huggingface.co/spaces/WideChaos/tensor-header-desk/commit/c1b5e505666747c7bad5d7015b87f9ccecdf2173).
